gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-006 gives a broad unsupported-correctness diagnosis, but does not identify the distinct failure that adding a level-chain can violate nested refinement-domain containment or require cross-level parent closure.

The gold bundles two independently diagnosable defects: the undefined unchecked_funcs state and the incomplete candidate-pair coverage after new corners are added. ISSUE-005 independently diagnoses and repairs the undefined state, while ISSUE-006 independently identifies the missing coverage argument for newly created pairs and the resulting termination/correctness gap.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The printed exact-mesh procedure lacks a complete, explicitly maintained unresolved-function/candidate-pair state: it is undefined as printed and, even if initialized only with new corners, can omit pairs between new corners and existing unresolved functions, so termination cannot certify that all problematic pairs were checked.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; the two entries use different demonstrations for the two distinct defects.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold entry contains distinct defects rather than one symptom: ISSUE-005 supplies a self-contained diagnosis of the undefined unchecked_funcs variable and its repair, while ISSUE-006 supplies a self-contained diagnosis of the separate failure to establish coverage of all newly created candidate pairs. Together they cover the full gold concern without adding an unstated logical connection.

component_coverage.gold_component: The main procedure uses unchecked_funcs without initializing or receiving it, so the next candidate-pair set is undefined and the algorithm is not executable as printed.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 explicitly identifies the uninitialized variable, the local-only computation, the undefined operation, and the required initialization/return repair.

component_coverage.gold_component: Initializing only with newly added corners omits pairs between a new corner and existing unresolved functions, so termination does not certify that all newly possible problematic pairs were examined.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-006 explicitly requires coverage of newly created pairs via the problematic-chain argument and identifies the missing checking-scheme justification as part of the unsupported guarantee.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-006 broadly questions the proof of the algorithm's guarantee but does not identify the specific omission of the finest-level iteration or the required creation of level L+1 data.

The gold defect is the initializer deleting pre-existing problematic pairs whose supports miss current marks. ISSUE-006 discusses the general checking proof and resolved-function skipping, but does not diagnose or repair this specific initializer deletion.

ISSUE-006 concerns missing correctness reasoning for the algorithm, but does not recognise that directly adjoining element marks can make the next domain fail the required union-of-closed-supports assumption or require support closure.

ISSUE-001 addresses a truncation-support implication in the THB admissibility proof. It does not identify the separate boundary-trace mismatch invalidating the vector-Laplace test's claimed space membership and exact reproduction.
